text: Three activities from earlier in this chapter, chained together into one real pipeline. Lookup reads the name of the table to copy this run, from a small configuration table. Copy moves that table's data from your SQL Server connection into Azure Blob Storage, using the exact table name the Lookup returned. And Stored Procedure logs the run's completion back into SQL Server once the copy actually succeeds.

Look up what to do, do it, record that it happened — a genuinely common real-world shape. The same three-part rhythm shows up constantly in production data engineering, just with different activities filling each role depending on the project.

Every activity you drag onto the canvas lands in the exact same authoring surface Lesson 11 already introduced. Drag each one in, connect them left to right, and configure each using exactly what the last five lessons already taught you, step by step.

Every connection between two activities on the canvas carries a dependency condition — Succeeded, Failed, Skipped, or Completed. This pipeline uses two of them on purpose: Copy to Stored Procedure on Succeeded, since logging completion only makes sense if the copy actually worked. And Copy to a Fail activity on Failed, so the pipeline stops loudly with a clear message instead of silently doing nothing at all.

Select Debug on the pipeline toolbar to run the whole thing immediately, with no publishing and no waiting on a trigger. Debug runs show their progress right on the canvas itself, and the same run details from the Monitor hub — a colored border on each activity as it runs, succeeds, or fails.

Every activity type this course touches from here forward builds on exactly this same pattern: drag an activity in, configure it, chain it to the next one with a dependency condition that genuinely means something. Chapter 3 complete. Next, Chapter 4: control flow and orchestration — parameters, variables, loops, and branching.
